letter_markdown:
# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date you are sending this letter]

**To:** Managed Health Services (MHS) — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Sawyer Iverson
[My street address]
[City, State, ZIP]
[My phone number]

**RE:** Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-02
**Member:** Sawyer Iverson
**Member ID:** W821798872
**Reference number:** POC-40E31914E1-52376
**Service denied:** Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
**Requesting surgeon:** Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery
**Governing policy:** 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of the knee arthroscopy and meniscus surgery (CPT 29881) that my surgeon, Reyes, MD, requested for me. The notice dated 2026-08-02 states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking MHS to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery.

I am writing because the records that were already submitted with the prior authorization request do address the plan's own criteria. Below, I set out the criteria in the plan's own words from the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines and match each one to what is in my chart. If something specific is still missing from my file, I am asking the plan to tell me and my surgeon exactly what it is, in writing, so we can send it.

## The plan's criteria and what my records show

**1. The plan's criterion:**

> "MRI demonstrates a bucket-handle tear of the meniscus and there is a history of acute injury/onset of symptoms with a locked knee and/or mechanical symptoms of locking or catching. (10)"

**My records:** My MRI of the knee on 2026-05-30 showed a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. My chart documents that I experience locking and giving way. This is the exact tear type and the exact mechanical symptom the plan names.

**2. The plan's criterion:**

> "Symptomatic meniscal tear confirmed by MRI results that demonstrate a peripheral tear in the vascular zone, root tear, (8) or other tear that the requesting physician considers repairable and is associated with pain localized to the corresponding compartment upon physical examination (9,10)"

**My records:** My MRI confirms a meniscal tear, and my exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this procedure is needed.

**3. The plan's criterion:**

> "MRI results confirm a frank meniscal tear (not simply degenerative changes, i.e., fraying) and the MRI does not demonstrate any of the following: moderate or severe articular cartilage thinning, full-thickness articular cartilage loss or defects, extrusion of the meniscus, subchondral edema, more than mild osteophytes, subchondral cysts, or an impression of 'moderate' or 'advanced/severe' arthritis"

**My records:** A displaced bucket-handle tear is a frank tear, not fraying or degenerative change. My MRI report describes the articular cartilage as preserved. None of the excluding findings the plan lists appear in my imaging report.

**4. The plan's criteria on arthritis grading:**

> "No Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3-4 changes on standing X-rays"

> "Weight-bearing X-rays (standing X-rays, Rosenberg view, 45-degree flexed PA view, etc.) demonstrate no moderate or severe osteoarthritic changes defined as Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3-4 (see Grading Appendix); X-rays should be described as showing either no arthritis or mild/minimal arthritis only (10)"

**My records:** My imaging is documented as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1. That is well below the Grade 3-4 level the plan excludes, and it falls within the "mild/minimal arthritis only" description the plan accepts.

**5. The plan's criterion on physical examination findings:**

> "When at least two of the following physical examination findings are present or there is at least one of the following physical examination findings and there is a history of mechanical symptoms such as 'catching' or 'locking' (9,10):"

The plan then lists findings including:

> "Knee joint line pain with forced hyperextension upon physical exam"

> "Knee joint line pain with maximum flexion upon physical exam"

> "Knee pain, crepitus, or an audible or palpable click with the McMurray’s test or Apley grind test"

> "Joint line tenderness to palpation upon physical exam"

**My records:** My exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side, and my history documents mechanical symptoms of locking and giving way. My MRI itself describes mechanical locking. If the plan needs my surgeon's exam findings named individually against this list, that is a specific, answerable request, and I am asking the plan to make it in writing rather than closing the file as incomplete.

**6. The plan's criteria on conservative treatment:**

> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least TWO of the following (11):"

The items from that list that I have available include:

> "Rest or activity modifications/limitations"

> "Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol"

**My records:** I completed supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion for 16 weeks, from 2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17, with 18 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I took NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief. My activity is limited — I cannot squat or kneel and am limited to level walking. My pain has been unrelieved by rest. My non-operative care therefore ran for 16 weeks and included both activity limitation and pharmacologic treatment with NSAIDs, without adequate relief.

**7. The plan's criterion on injections:**

> "No intra-articular cortisone injections within 4 weeks of surgery (1–3)"

**My records:** My corticosteroid injection was on 2026-04-19 and gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. That date is months before any anticipated surgery date, so this exclusion does not apply to me.

**8. The plan's criterion on symptom duration:**

> "At least 12 weeks of knee pain with documented loss of function"

**My records:** I have had 14 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest. My loss of function is documented: locking and giving way, inability to squat or kneel, and limitation to level walking. Fourteen months is far more than the 12 weeks the plan requires.

**9. One criterion that does not apply to me:**

> "MRI demonstrates a meniscus tear (9,10) in a patient age <21 years who complains of pain or mechanical symptoms or has ANY positive meniscal findings on physical examination"

I note this criterion only for completeness. I am not relying on it, and I am not claiming it applies to me.

## A note on the policy text I have

I want to be straightforward with the reviewer: several of the criteria I quoted above end with a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that I was not able to obtain in full. I have quoted only the policy language I actually have, word for word, and I have not guessed at or reconstructed any part of the policy I do not have in front of me. Where the plan's guidelines list additional conditions I have not reproduced, I am not characterizing them.

## Request for the criteria the plan actually applied

The denial states that the documentation was incomplete, but it does not identify which specific criterion was unmet or which specific document was missing. MHS holds the clinical review criteria that were applied to my request, and I am asking the plan to provide them to me in writing. Specifically, I request:

- the name and version of the medical policy and clinical review criteria used to review CPT 29881 for me;
- the specific criterion or criteria the reviewer found unmet;
- an itemized list of the documents or findings the reviewer considered missing; and
- the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made this determination.

I understand my plan uses Evolent for musculoskeletal surgery review, and that the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines are published without a login at the address listed at the top of this letter. If a different document or a different section was applied to my case, I ask that the plan identify it.

## Closing

My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed. The records already in my file show a displaced bucket-handle tear on MRI, preserved articular cartilage, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1, mechanical locking and giving way, 14 months of pain, and 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy plus 4 months of NSAIDs without adequate relief. Each of those facts lines up with language the plan itself publishes.

I respectfully ask MHS to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-02 and approve knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask for a written explanation identifying the exact criterion that was not met and the exact documentation that would satisfy it, along with information about my right to further review.

**Deadline and submission:** My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-01-29**. I am submitting this appeal to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand that appeals for this plan are handled by state: an appeal or grievance form is available at ambetterhealth.com by selecting Indiana, and I can also call the number on my member ID card. My denial letter is the authoritative source for the deadline and the submission address, and I am following it.

Please send all correspondence about this appeal to me at the address above, with a copy to Reyes, MD.

Thank you for reviewing this again.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
**Sawyer Iverson**
Member ID: W821798872
Reference number: POC-40E31914E1-52376
[My phone number]
[My email address]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-02
- MRI report dated 2026-05-30
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17, 18 visits)
- Office notes from Reyes, MD
- [Any other records I am including]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
